"Category	Final specification
Title	Street Legends
Genre	2D arcade fighting
Perspective	Side-view
Orientation	Landscape
Art	Detailed 16-bit pixel art
Game mode	Single-player
Fighters	4 at launch, 8 planned
Arenas	7
Round length	60 seconds
Match format	First to 2 rounds
Economy	Earnable coins
Shop	Outfits, accessories, finishing moves
Price	$0.99 one-time purchase
Advertisements	None
Download target	50–80 MB
Maximum download goal	Under 100 MB STREET LEGENDS
COMPLETE GAME DEVELOPMENT SPECIFICATION

PROJECT TYPE: 2D MOBILE ARCADE FIGHTING GAME

DEVELOPMENT PRIORITY: Create a complete, playable, polished, lightweight fighting game with functional systems. Do not create merely a visual demonstration or a collection of disconnected menus.

================================================== SECTION 1: GAME IDENTITY AND PURPOSE

Create an original 2D pixel-art fighting game titled STREET LEGENDS.

The game is inspired by classic arcade fighting games from the 1990s, featuring large character sprites, responsive fighting mechanics, exciting combat animations, unique fighting arenas, character customization, and a championship progression system.

The game must be designed primarily for mobile devices.

GAME REQUIREMENTS:

2D side-view fighting perspective.
Landscape screen orientation.
Single-player gameplay against computer-controlled opponents.
Detailed 16-bit pixel-art graphics.
Four playable fighters in the initial release.
Eight fighters planned for the expanded roster.
Seven different fighting arenas.
An in-game currency system.
A fully functional cosmetic shop.
Character outfits, accessories, and finishing moves.
Local save functionality.
No advertisements.
No additional real-money purchases.

The initial game must feel like a complete product rather than an unfinished prototype.

================================================== SECTION 2: GRAPHICS AND VISUAL DESIGN

ART STYLE:

Use detailed 16-bit pixel art inspired by classic arcade fighting games.

Do not make the fighters excessively small.

CHARACTER DIMENSIONS:

Target character height: 180–240 pixels.
Target character width: 100–150 pixels.
Characters should have detailed faces, clothing, hairstyles, body proportions, and recognizable silhouettes.
Fighters must remain clearly visible during combat.
Characters should occupy a substantial portion of the fighting screen.

ANIMATION:

Create individual animations for:

Idle stance.
Walking forward.
Walking backward.
Running, if supported.
Jumping.
Landing.
Crouching.
Punching.
Kicking.
Blocking.
Taking damage.
Knockback.
Knockdown.
Getting back up.
Special attacks.
Finishing moves.
Victory.
Defeat.

Animations must be smooth and consistent.

Do not use a single static image for every character action.

VISUAL QUALITY:

Consistent pixel-art resolution.
Sharp character outlines.
Detailed environments.
Coordinated color palettes.
No blurry or distorted sprites.
No stretched character proportions.
No overlapping character sprites unless an attack animation requires it.
================================================== SECTION 3: PLAYABLE CHARACTERS

The initial release must include four original playable fighters.

FIGHTER 1: KENJI

Fighting style: Karate.

Appearance:

Black hair.
Red headband.
White karate uniform.
Traditional martial arts appearance.

Combat characteristics:

Balanced movement speed.
Balanced attack strength.
Reliable punching and kicking combinations.
Beginner-friendly fighting style.

Special move: Dragon Strike.

FIGHTER 2: MAYA

Fighting style: Kickboxing.

Appearance:

Athletic female fighter.
Purple fighting outfit.
Distinctive hairstyle.
Sport-inspired appearance.

Combat characteristics:

Fast movement.
Fast kicking combinations.
Strong aerial attacks.
Lower individual attack damage than heavy fighters.

Special move: Cyclone Kick.

FIGHTER 3: BRUNO

Fighting style: Boxing.

Appearance:

Large muscular male fighter.
Boxing gloves.
Blue boxing shorts.

Combat characteristics:

Powerful punches.
High individual attack damage.
Slower movement.
Strong defensive abilities.

Special move: Heavy Impact.

FIGHTER 4: AKARI

Fighting style: Ninja martial arts.

Appearance:

Female ninja.
Dark green fighting outfit.
Mask or face covering.
Distinctive ninja hairstyle.

Combat characteristics:

Fast movement.
Quick attacks.
Evasive fighting style.
Special attack combinations.

Special move: Shadow Rush.

CHARACTER BALANCING:

Each fighter must have individual statistics:

Health.
Movement speed.
Attack strength.
Defense.
Jump height.
Special attack strength.

No character should be overwhelmingly stronger than all other characters.

Create unique character animations and attack effects.

FUTURE ROSTER:

Design the game architecture to support eight fighters eventually.

The initial version should contain four fully implemented fighters. The remaining four can be introduced in a future content update without requiring a complete game rebuild.

================================================== SECTION 4: FIGHTING MECHANICS

The game must feature one-versus-one combat.

CAMERA:

Side-view fighting camera.
Keep both fighters visible.
Follow character movement when necessary.
Prevent characters from leaving the playable arena.
Maintain a consistent fighting distance and screen composition.

PLAYER CONTROLS:

Include large touchscreen buttons suitable for mobile devices.

LEFT: Move left.

RIGHT: Move right.

UP: Jump.

DOWN: Crouch.

PUNCH: Perform a quick punching attack.

KICK: Perform a kicking attack.

BLOCK: Defend against incoming attacks.

SPECIAL: Perform the fighter's unique special move when enough special energy is available.

CONTROLS MUST:

Respond immediately to touch.
Support holding directional buttons.
Avoid accidental simultaneous inputs.
Have clear visual feedback.
Be comfortable on smaller mobile screens.

COMBAT SYSTEM:

Implement:

Real attack hitboxes.
Collision detection.
Health reduction.
Attack cooldowns.
Block damage reduction.
Knockback.
Stun reactions.
Jump attacks.
Ground attacks.
Special attacks.
Combo detection.
Victory and defeat conditions.

Attacks must connect only when the opponent is within the appropriate attack range.

Prevent attacks from damaging opponents across the entire screen.

SPECIAL ATTACK METER:

Include a special energy meter for each fighter.

The meter should increase through successful attacks and taking damage.

Once sufficient energy is available, the player can activate the character's special move.

Special moves must have unique visual effects and animations.

================================================== SECTION 5: MATCH RULES

Each match consists of up to three rounds.

Each round lasts 60 seconds.
The first fighter to win two rounds wins the match.
Both fighters begin each round with full health.
A knockout occurs when a fighter's health reaches zero.
If time expires, the fighter with more remaining health wins.
If health is equal, use a short overtime or another fair tie-breaking rule.

DISPLAY:

Player health bar.
Opponent health bar.
Countdown timer.
Round indicator.
Special energy meter.
Fighter names.
Victory and defeat notifications.

The game must correctly track rounds and determine the match winner.

================================================== SECTION 6: COMPUTER-CONTROLLED OPPONENTS

Create an AI opponent system.

The opponent must be able to:

Approach the player.
Maintain fighting distance.
Attack.
Block.
Jump.
Crouch.
Use special moves.
React to incoming attacks.
Defend when necessary.
Attempt combinations.

DIFFICULTY LEVELS:

EASY:

Less aggressive.
Slower reactions.
More opportunities for the player to attack.

NORMAL:

Balanced attacking and defending.
Reasonable reaction speed.
Moderate combinations.

HARD:

More aggressive.
Better defensive reactions.
More effective combinations.
More frequent special attacks.

AI should not cheat by automatically knowing every player input or ignoring attack cooldowns.

================================================== SECTION 7: SEVEN FIGHTING ARENAS

Create seven visually different fighting stages.

Each stage must use detailed pixel-art backgrounds and remain optimized for mobile performance.

ARENA 1: NEON CITY

Appearance:

Modern city street at night.
Colorful neon signs.
Buildings.
Streetlights.
Urban atmosphere.

Subtle animation:

Flickering neon signs.
Moving background lights.

Availability:

Unlocked immediately.

ARENA 2: DRAGON DOJO

Appearance:

Traditional Japanese training hall.
Wooden floor.
Lanterns.
Decorative architecture.

Subtle animation:

Moving lantern light.
Gentle environmental effects.

Unlock:

Win three matches.

ARENA 3: SUNSET BEACH

Appearance:

Tropical beach.
Ocean.
Palm trees.
Sunset sky.

Subtle animation:

Moving ocean waves.
Palm leaves moving in the wind.

Unlock:

Win six matches.

ARENA 4: UNDERGROUND

Appearance:

Dark industrial warehouse.
Concrete walls.
Metal structures.
Underground fighting atmosphere.

Subtle animation:

Flickering lights.
Steam or environmental effects.

Unlock:

Win ten matches.

ARENA 5: SKY HIGH

Appearance:

City rooftop.
Large city skyline.
Buildings in the distance.
Nighttime atmosphere.

Subtle animation:

Moving clouds.
Distant city lights.

Unlock:

Win fifteen matches.

ARENA 6: FORGOTTEN TEMPLE

Appearance:

Ancient temple.
Mountain scenery.
Stone architecture.
Traditional decorations.

Subtle animation:

Moving leaves.
Gentle environmental effects.

Unlock:

Complete championship mode.

ARENA 7: THE COLOSSEUM

Appearance:

Ancient Roman gladiator arena.
Massive stone structures.
Spectator stands.
Roman banners.
Large cheering crowd.
Warm sunset lighting.

Subtle animation:

Cheering spectators.
Moving banners.
Environmental lighting effects.

Unlock:

Defeat the final championship boss.

ARENA REQUIREMENTS:

Every arena must have:

A distinct visual identity.
A separate background.
Proper fighting floor positioning.
Correct character scaling.
Unobstructed combat space.
Appropriate background music or ambient audio where practical.

Players must be able to revisit previously unlocked arenas.

================================================== SECTION 8: CHAMPIONSHIP MODE

Create a single-player championship mode.

The player selects one fighter and enters a fighting tournament.

The tournament must feature increasingly difficult opponents.

Include:

Tournament introduction.
Opponent presentation.
Individual fights.
Progression between matches.
Championship final.
Final victory screen.

The final boss should have stronger AI and a more challenging fighting style.

The Colosseum becomes available after the final boss is defeated.

The player must be able to replay championship mode.

Save championship completion and progression.

================================================== SECTION 9: COIN AND REWARD SYSTEM

Create a permanent in-game currency called LEGEND COINS.

Players earn coins by playing matches.

REWARDS:

Normal victory: 250 coins.

Victory without losing a round: 400 coins.

Perfect victory without taking damage: 600 coins.

Championship completion: 2,000 bonus coins.

Final boss defeat: 1,000 bonus coins.

Reward conditions must be checked correctly.

Do not award duplicate rewards from repeatedly opening a results screen.

The player's coin balance must be saved permanently.

The player must not lose coins when losing a match.

================================================== SECTION 10: IN-GAME SHOP

Create a shop called LEGENDS MARKET.

The shop must be fully functional.

The shop should have three main categories.

CATEGORY A: FIGHTER OUTFITS

Examples:

Alternate fighter costumes.
Different clothing colors.
Special outfits.
Rare outfits.
Exclusive championship costumes.

Suggested prices:

Standard alternate outfit: 1,000 coins.
Rare outfit: 2,500 coins.
Exclusive costume: 7,500 coins.

CATEGORY B: ACCESSORIES

Examples:

Gloves.
Boots.
Headbands.
Masks.
Hairstyles.

Suggested prices:

Gloves: 500 coins.
Boots: 750 coins.
Hairstyle: 800 coins.

CATEGORY C: FINISHING MOVES

Create unique finishing animations for fighters.

Examples:

Special knockout animations.
Unique final punches.
Unique final kicks.
Character-specific victory sequences.

Suggested price:

Special finishing move: 5,000 coins.

SHOP FUNCTIONALITY:

The player must be able to:

Browse categories.
View items.
Preview cosmetics.
See item prices.
Check their coin balance.
Purchase items.
Receive a purchase confirmation.
Equip unlocked items.
Unequip items.
Revisit purchased items.

PURCHASE RULES:

All items must be purchased using earned Legend Coins.
No additional real-money purchases.
No paid loot boxes.
No advertisements.
No subscriptions.
No randomized paid rewards.
No duplicate purchases for already owned items.

Purchased items must remain permanently unlocked.

The shop must never subtract coins without completing a successful purchase.

================================================== SECTION 11: MAIN MENU AND GAME INTERFACE

Create an attractive retro arcade main menu.

MAIN MENU OPTIONS:

PLAY
CHAMPIONSHIP
FIGHTERS
LEGENDS MARKET
ARENA SELECT
SETTINGS

The main menu should display:

Street Legends logo.
Animated fighter artwork.
Player coin balance.
Clear navigation buttons.

CHARACTER SELECTION:

Display all available fighters.

Show:

Fighter portrait.
Fighter name.
Fighting style.
Statistics.
Special move.
Locked or unlocked status.

Allow the player to preview a character before choosing.

ARENA SELECTION:

Display the seven arenas.

Show:

Arena preview.
Arena name.
Unlock requirement.
Locked or unlocked status.

RESULTS SCREEN:

After every match, display:

Winner.
Loser.
Rounds won.
Match performance.
Coins earned.
Updated coin balance.

Include buttons for:

Rematch.
Return to main menu.
Continue championship, when applicable.
================================================== SECTION 12: SOUND AND MUSIC

Include:

Main menu music.
Fighting music.
Different music or ambient sound for arenas where possible.
Punch sound effects.
Kick sound effects.
Blocking sound effects.
Jump sound effects.
Knockout sound effects.
Victory music.
Defeat music.
Menu navigation sounds.
Shop purchase confirmation sounds.

Audio must be compressed and optimized.

Include separate volume controls for:

Music.
Sound effects.

Allow players to mute audio.

Use original or properly licensed audio assets.

================================================== SECTION 13: SAVE SYSTEM

Create a reliable local save system.

Save:

Player coin balance.
Unlocked characters.
Purchased outfits.
Purchased accessories.
Purchased finishing moves.
Equipped cosmetics.
Unlocked arenas.
Championship completion.
Match progression.
Settings.
Sound preferences.

Progress must remain saved after:

Closing the game.
Restarting the application.
Losing a match.
Returning to the main menu.

Use appropriate local storage for the development platform.

Avoid resetting player progress when entering a new match.

Handle interrupted purchases and interrupted matches safely.

================================================== SECTION 14: MONETIZATION AND APP STORE MODEL

BUSINESS MODEL:

The game must be sold for a one-time purchase price of $0.99.

This price is intended for the initial App Store release and must be configured through the appropriate store listing and pricing system.

The game must be a complete premium product.

STRICT MONETIZATION RULES:

No advertisements.
No rewarded advertisements.
No banner advertisements.
No forced video advertisements.
No additional paid characters.
No additional paid outfits.
No paid finishing moves.
No subscriptions.
No additional in-game real-money purchases.

All cosmetic items must be obtainable through gameplay and Legend Coins.

The game should be playable offline after installation wherever the platform permits.

Do not introduce advertising SDKs or unnecessary third-party services.

================================================== SECTION 15: DOWNLOAD SIZE AND PERFORMANCE

The game must be lightweight.

TARGET DOWNLOAD SIZE: 50–80 MB.

MAXIMUM TARGET: Under 100 MB.

This is a target that must be verified after export, not an assumed result.

OPTIMIZATION:

Compress image assets.
Use optimized pixel-art spritesheets.
Reuse suitable visual assets.
Compress music and sound effects.
Avoid unnecessary video files.
Avoid unnecessary high-resolution textures.
Remove unused assets.
Avoid unnecessarily large libraries.
Optimize animations and backgrounds.

Do not sacrifice fighter detail to reduce file size.

PERFORMANCE:

Target 60 FPS on supported devices.
Maintain responsive touchscreen controls.
Avoid excessive memory usage.
Prevent unnecessary loading screens.
Keep gameplay smooth.
Avoid crashes during matches or shop interactions.
================================================== SECTION 16: MOBILE USER EXPERIENCE

Design the entire interface for mobile devices.

Requirements:

Landscape orientation.
Readable text.
Large touchscreen buttons.
Appropriate spacing.
Clear health bars.
Visible countdown timer.
Easy-to-use menus.
Responsive layout.
Proper screen scaling.

Do not place important buttons too close to screen edges.

Ensure the controls do not cover the fighters.

================================================== SECTION 17: QUALITY ASSURANCE AND TESTING

Before considering the game complete, test every major feature.

COMBAT TESTS:

Movement works in both directions.
Jumping works.
Crouching works.
Punches connect correctly.
Kicks connect correctly.
Blocking works.
Special moves activate correctly.
Health decreases correctly.
Knockouts work.
Match winners are determined correctly.
Round progression works.

AI TESTS:

Opponents move.
Opponents attack.
Opponents defend.
Opponents use special moves.
Difficulty levels behave differently.

SHOP TESTS:

Coins are awarded correctly.
Coins are saved.
Purchases work.
Insufficient funds prevent purchases.
Owned items cannot be purchased twice.
Cosmetics can be equipped.
Cosmetics remain unlocked after restarting.

ARENA TESTS:

All seven backgrounds load correctly.
Unlock requirements work.
Locked arenas cannot be entered.
Unlocked arenas can be replayed.

SAVE TESTS:

Close and reopen the game.
Confirm coin balance remains correct.
Confirm purchases remain unlocked.
Confirm arena progression remains saved.
Confirm championship completion remains saved.

PERFORMANCE TESTS:

Check for crashes.
Check for missing assets.
Check for distorted sprites.
Check for broken animations.
Check mobile controls.
Measure the exported installation size.
================================================== SECTION 18: DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES

Build the game in the following order.

PHASE 1: Create the core fighting engine, player movement, attacks, hit detection, health bars, timer, and AI opponent.

PHASE 2: Create the four initial fighters with their unique appearances, animations, statistics, and special moves.

PHASE 3: Create all seven arenas and the arena selection system.

PHASE 4: Create the championship tournament and final boss.

PHASE 5: Create Legend Coins, match rewards, and the complete Legends Market.

PHASE 6: Implement outfit customization, accessories, and finishing moves.

PHASE 7: Create the main menu, character selection, results screens, audio, and settings.

PHASE 8: Implement permanent saving and loading.

PHASE 9: Optimize assets, test gameplay, fix bugs, and export the final mobile build.

IMPORTANT DEVELOPMENT INSTRUCTIONS:

Do not skip requested features.
Do not replace functional mechanics with decorative buttons.
Do not create fake shop purchases.
Do not make every fighter look identical.
Do not use tiny character sprites.
Do not remove any of the seven arenas.
Do not add advertisements.
Do not add additional real-money purchases.
Do not sacrifice gameplay quality for unnecessary visual effects.

If a requested feature cannot be implemented by the available development tools, clearly identify the limitation rather than pretending the feature works.

Prioritize a stable, complete, playable game over unnecessary complexity.

FINAL GOAL:

Deliver STREET LEGENDS as a polished, lightweight, premium 2D arcade fighting game with large detailed pixel-art fighters, responsive combat, seven unique arenas, a championship mode, an earnable coin economy, and a fully functional cosmetic shop.

The game should feel like a complete classic arcade fighting experience redesigned for modern mobile devices.Character size: The fighters must actually look large on the screen. Don't let the AI interpret pixel art as tiny 32 × 32 characters.
The shop: Make sure purchases, coin deductions, and saved outfits work. A shop that only looks attractive isn't enough.
Seven arenas: Check that all seven are separate selectable stages, not seven names attached to the same background.
File size: Check the exported build, not just the project size displayed inside the editor.
4. A realistic development expectation


If it struggles, prioritize these features in order:

Working one-versus-one combat.
Four functional fighters.
Seven backgrounds.
Championship progression.
Working coin system.
Working shop.
Cosmetics and finishing moves.Category	Number
Male fighters	10
Female fighters	10
Total playable fighters	20
Initially available	4
Unlockable	16MAJOR ROSTER EXPANSION: 20 PLAYABLE FIGHTERS

Expand STREET LEGENDS to feature a complete roster of 20 original playable fighters.

ROSTER COMPOSITION:

10 male fighters.
10 female fighters.
All characters must be adults.
All characters must have unique appearances.
All characters must have individual fighting styles.
All characters must have their own special moves.
All characters must be selectable and playable.

MALE FIGHTERS:

Kenji — Karate — Dragon Strike.
Bruno — Boxing — Heavy Impact.
Jae — Taekwondo — Lightning Kick.
Marcus — Street Fighting — Ground Breaker.
Ryuji — Kenjutsu — Blade Dance.
Axel — Kickboxing — Rapid Assault.
Titan — Wrestling — Titan Slam.
Liang — Kung Fu — Dragon Combination.
Dante — Capoeira — Spinning Tempest.
Vex — Dark Martial Arts — Shadow Burst.

FEMALE FIGHTERS:

Maya — Kickboxing — Cyclone Kick.
Akari — Ninjutsu — Shadow Rush.
Scarlett — Boxing — Crimson Knockout.
Nia — Taekwondo — Skybreaker.
Mei — Kung Fu — Golden Dragon.
Isabella — Capoeira — Tropical Storm.
Raven — Wrestling — Raven's Wrath.
Yuna — Kenjutsu — Moonlight Strike.
Vanessa — Street Fighting — Street Fury.
Seraphina — Mystic Martial Arts — Celestial Burst.

CHARACTER APPEARANCE:

Create visually attractive, detailed and recognizable adult characters.

Female character design:

Attractive facial features.
Distinctive hairstyles.
Athletic physiques.
Stylish fighting outfits.
Individual color palettes.
Detailed clothing and accessories.
Confident and memorable personalities.

Male character design:

Distinctive facial features.
Different hairstyles.
Varied body types.
Detailed fighting uniforms and streetwear.
Unique fighting stances.
Individual color palettes.

Do not make characters look identical.

Do not simply recolor one character sprite to create another fighter.

CHARACTER ANIMATIONS:

Every fighter must have:

Idle animation.
Walking animation.
Jumping animation.
Crouching animation.
Punch animation.
Kick animation.
Blocking animation.
Hit reaction.
Knockdown animation.
Getting-up animation.
Special attack animation.
Finishing move animation.
Victory animation.
Defeat animation.

Every fighter must have unique special attacks and recognizable finishing moves.

CHARACTER STATISTICS:

Each character must have individual:

Health.
Attack strength.
Defense.
Movement speed.
Jump height.
Special attack power.

Ensure balanced competitive gameplay.

UNLOCK SYSTEM:

Four fighters are available initially: Kenji, Bruno, Maya and Akari.

The remaining 16 fighters must be unlockable through gameplay.

Use championship progression and Legend Coins to unlock fighters.

Display locked characters in the character selection menu.

Show each locked fighter's name, portrait, fighting style and unlock requirement.

Do not charge real money for fighters.

CUSTOMIZATION:

Every fighter should support at least two additional unlockable outfits.

Allow players to equip outfits and accessories from Legends Market.

Outfits must not change character hitboxes, damage values or competitive balance.

IMPORTANT TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS:

Create individual character assets.
Use optimized spritesheets.
Reuse suitable animation infrastructure without making characters visually identical.
Maintain consistent sprite scale.
Preserve large, detailed character appearances.
Optimize character assets to help keep the total game installation below 100 MB.

All 20 fighters must be included in the final playable roster.

Do not silently reduce the roster to four or eight characters.

If the development environment cannot generate all 20 at once, build them in organized batches while preserving the complete 20-character roster design and character selection system.Touchscreen Controls – Essential Requirement

Create a fully functional, responsive touchscreen control layout for mobile devices in landscape orientation.

Left side – Movement controls
Add a large virtual directional joystick on the bottom-left of the screen.
The joystick must support moving left, right, jumping (up), and crouching (down).
Alternatively, provide four separate directional arrow buttons if a virtual joystick is not supported.
The joystick must respond smoothly and immediately to finger movement.
Keep it fixed in position so players can easily reach it with their left thumb.
Right side – Action buttons

Add four large, clearly labeled arcade-style buttons:

X – Punch: Fast standard punch attack.
A – Kick: Standard kick attack.
B – Block: Hold to defend against incoming attacks.
Y – Special: Perform the character's unique special move when enough special meter is available.

Buttons must respond to touch and support holding where appropriate. Each button must trigger its assigned fighting action reliably.

Additional requirements
Display all controls directly over the gameplay screen.
Use large, clearly visible buttons with distinct colors and recognizable labels.
Make buttons comfortable to press without accidentally touching neighboring buttons.
Allow simultaneous inputs where appropriate, such as moving while attacking or jumping while kicking.
Prevent controls from covering the fighters, health bars, timer, or important gameplay information.
Make the control layout scale correctly across different phone and tablet screen sizes.
Provide an option in Settings to adjust control size and transparency.
Ensure controls work through actual touchscreen input, not just keyboard simulation.
Do not require a physical controller or keyboard to play.
Test every control on a real touchscreen device before release.Fighter Collision, Solid Movement and Living Environments
1. Solid Fighter Collision – Essential

Characters must behave like solid physical objects during combat.

Fighters must never walk through, overlap, or pass through each other.
Implement proper collision detection and collision boundaries between both fighters.
When fighters approach each other, they must stop at a realistic fighting distance.
If one fighter pushes toward the other, prevent them from moving through their opponent.
Characters must maintain consistent ground positioning and must not slide, teleport, or randomly drift.
Jumping, crouching, blocking, attacking, knockbacks, and special moves must respect collision rules.
Knockback animations must not cause fighters to pass through one another.
Prevent fighters from leaving the playable arena boundaries.
Ensure collision detection works consistently at different frame rates.
Use separate attack hitboxes and character collision boxes so attacks can connect without sprites physically passing through each other.
Both fighters must remain properly grounded unless jumping or being knocked into the air.
2. Living Backgrounds and Environmental Animations

Make every arena feel alive instead of using completely static backgrounds.

Add subtle environmental animations that do not interfere with fighting or reduce performance.

Examples:

Birds flying across the sky and occasionally landing on rooftops.
Birds taking off from buildings and flying away.
Clouds slowly moving across the sky.
Trees, palm leaves, and plants gently moving in the wind.
Streetlights flickering and neon signs glowing.
Windows and buildings displaying changing lights.
Ocean waves moving and crashing on the beach.
Flags and banners gently waving.
Dust, steam, and leaves moving through appropriate environments.
Background spectators occasionally cheering, clapping, and moving.

Each arena should have environmental animations appropriate to its setting. Do not simply reuse the same background effects everywhere.

3. Dynamic Day and Night Cycle

Implement a visual day-and-night cycle for arenas.

Gradually transition between morning, daytime, evening, sunset, and nighttime.
Change the sky color, lighting, shadows, and environmental atmosphere.
The sun should move across the sky during daytime.
The sun should set and the moon should appear at night.
Stars should become visible in suitable nighttime environments.
Clouds should continue moving during the cycle.
City lights and streetlights should turn on as darkness approaches and turn off during daylight.
Beach sunsets should have changing sky colors and lighting.
Background environments should visually respond to the time of day.
4. Cycle Settings and Performance
Allow players to select a fixed time of day or enable automatic day/night cycling.
Make transitions gradual and smooth, not sudden.
Keep the fighting area bright enough to see characters and attacks clearly.
Environmental animations must never interfere with combat hitboxes or controls.
Optimize background animations to maintain the target 60 FPS.
Do not sacrifice fighter sprite quality or animation detail for background effects.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

COMPLETE GAME DEVELOPMENT SPECIFICATION

PROJECT TYPE: 2D MOBILE ARCADE FIGHTING GAME

DEVELOPMENT PRIORITY: Create a complete, playable, polished, lightweight fighting game with functional systems. Do not create merely a visual demonstration or a collection of disconnected menus.

================================================== SECTION 1: GAME IDENTITY AND PURPOSE

Create an original 2D pixel-art fighting game titled STREET LEGENDS.

The game is inspired by classic arcade fighting games from the 1990s, featuring large character sprites, responsive fighting mechanics, exciting combat animations, unique fighting arenas, character customization, and a championship progression system.

The game must be designed primarily for mobile devices.

GAME REQUIREMENTS:

2D side-view fighting perspective.
Landscape screen orientation.
Single-player gameplay against computer-controlled opponents.
Detailed 16-bit pixel-art graphics.
Four playable fighters in the initial release.
Eight fighters planned for the expanded roster.
Seven different fighting arenas.
An in-game currency system.
A fully functional cosmetic shop.
Character outfits, accessories, and finishing moves.
Local save functionality.
No advertisements.
No additional real-money purchases.

The initial game must feel like a complete product rather than an unfinished prototype.

================================================== SECTION 2: GRAPHICS AND VISUAL DESIGN

ART STYLE:

Use detailed 16-bit pixel art inspired by classic arcade fighting games.

Do not make the fighters excessively small.

CHARACTER DIMENSIONS:

Target character height: 180–240 pixels.
Target character width: 100–150 pixels.
Characters should have detailed faces, clothing, hairstyles, body proportions, and recognizable silhouettes.
Fighters must remain clearly visible during combat.
Characters should occupy a substantial portion of the fighting screen.

ANIMATION:

Create individual animations for:

Idle stance.
Walking forward.
Walking backward.
Running, if supported.
Jumping.
Landing.
Crouching.
Punching.
Kicking.
Blocking.
Taking damage.
Knockback.
Knockdown.
Getting back up.
Special attacks.
Finishing moves.
Victory.
Defeat.

Animations must be smooth and consistent.

Do not use a single static image for every character action.

VISUAL QUALITY:

Consistent pixel-art resolution.
Sharp character outlines.
Detailed environments.
Coordinated color palettes.
No blurry or distorted sprites.
No stretched character proportions.
No overlapping character sprites unless an attack animation requires it.
================================================== SECTION 3: PLAYABLE CHARACTERS

The initial release must include four original playable fighters.

FIGHTER 1: KENJI

Fighting style: Karate.

Appearance:

Black hair.
Red headband.
White karate uniform.
Traditional martial arts appearance.

Combat characteristics:

Balanced movement speed.
Balanced attack strength.
Reliable punching and kicking combinations.
Beginner-friendly fighting style.

Special move: Dragon Strike.

FIGHTER 2: MAYA

Fighting style: Kickboxing.

Appearance:

Athletic female fighter.
Purple fighting outfit.
Distinctive hairstyle.
Sport-inspired appearance.

Combat characteristics:

Fast movement.
Fast kicking combinations.
Strong aerial attacks.
Lower individual attack damage than heavy fighters.

Special move: Cyclone Kick.

FIGHTER 3: BRUNO

Fighting style: Boxing.

Appearance:

Large muscular male fighter.
Boxing gloves.
Blue boxing shorts.

Combat characteristics:

Powerful punches.
High individual attack damage.
Slower movement.
Strong defensive abilities.

Special move: Heavy Impact.

FIGHTER 4: AKARI

Fighting style: Ninja martial arts.

Appearance:

Female ninja.
Dark green fighting outfit.
Mask or face covering.
Distinctive ninja hairstyle.

Combat characteristics:

Fast movement.
Quick attacks.
Evasive fighting style.
Special attack combinations.

Special move: Shadow Rush.

CHARACTER BALANCING:

Each fighter must have individual statistics:

Health.
Movement speed.
Attack strength.
Defense.
Jump height.
Special attack strength.

No character should be overwhelmingly stronger than all other characters.

Create unique character animations and attack effects.

FUTURE ROSTER:

Design the game architecture to support eight fighters eventually.

The initial version should contain four fully implemented fighters. The remaining four can be introduced in a future content update without requiring a complete game rebuild.

================================================== SECTION 4: FIGHTING MECHANICS

The game must feature one-versus-one combat.

CAMERA:

Side-view fighting camera.
Keep both fighters visible.
Follow character movement when necessary.
Prevent characters from leaving the playable arena.
Maintain a consistent fighting distance and screen composition.

PLAYER CONTROLS:

Include large touchscreen buttons suitable for mobile devices.

LEFT: Move left.

RIGHT: Move right.

UP: Jump.

DOWN: Crouch.

PUNCH: Perform a quick punching attack.

KICK: Perform a kicking attack.

BLOCK: Defend against incoming attacks.

SPECIAL: Perform the fighter's unique special move when enough special energy is available.

CONTROLS MUST:

Respond immediately to touch.
Support holding directional buttons.
Avoid accidental simultaneous inputs.
Have clear visual feedback.
Be comfortable on smaller mobile screens.

COMBAT SYSTEM:

Implement:

Real attack hitboxes.
Collision detection.
Health reduction.
Attack cooldowns.
Block damage reduction.
Knockback.
Stun reactions.
Jump attacks.
Ground attacks.
Special attacks.
Combo detection.
Victory and defeat conditions.

Attacks must connect only when the opponent is within the appropriate attack range.

Prevent attacks from damaging opponents across the entire screen.

SPECIAL ATTACK METER:

Include a special energy meter for each fighter.

The meter should increase through successful attacks and taking damage.

Once sufficient energy is available, the player can activate the character's special move.

Special moves must have unique visual effects and animations.

================================================== SECTION 5: MATCH RULES

Each match consists of up to three rounds.

Each round lasts 60 seconds.
The first fighter to win two rounds wins the match.
Both fighters begin each round with full health.
A knockout occurs when a fighter's health reaches zero.
If time expires, the fighter with more remaining health wins.
If health is equal, use a short overtime or another fair tie-breaking rule.

DISPLAY:

Player health bar.
Opponent health bar.
Countdown timer.
Round indicator.
Special energy meter.
Fighter names.
Victory and defeat notifications.

The game must correctly track rounds and determine the match winner.

================================================== SECTION 6: COMPUTER-CONTROLLED OPPONENTS

Create an AI opponent system.

The opponent must be able to:

Approach the player.
Maintain fighting distance.
Attack.
Block.
Jump.
Crouch.
Use special moves.
React to incoming attacks.
Defend when necessary.
Attempt combinations.

DIFFICULTY LEVELS:

EASY:

Less aggressive.
Slower reactions.
More opportunities for the player to attack.

NORMAL:

Balanced attacking and defending.
Reasonable reaction speed.
Moderate combinations.

HARD:

More aggressive.
Better defensive reactions.
More effective combinations.
More frequent special attacks.

AI should not cheat by automatically knowing every player input or ignoring attack cooldowns.

================================================== SECTION 7: SEVEN FIGHTING ARENAS

Create seven visually different fighting stages.

Each stage must use detailed pixel-art backgrounds and remain optimized for mobile performance.

ARENA 1: NEON CITY

Appearance:

Modern city street at night.
Colorful neon signs.
Buildings.
Streetlights.
Urban atmosphere.

Subtle animation:

Flickering neon signs.
Moving background lights.

Availability:

Unlocked immediately.

ARENA 2: DRAGON DOJO

Appearance:

Traditional Japanese training hall.
Wooden floor.
Lanterns.
Decorative architecture.

Subtle animation:

Moving lantern light.
Gentle environmental effects.

Unlock:

Win three matches.

ARENA 3: SUNSET BEACH

Appearance:

Tropical beach.
Ocean.
Palm trees.
Sunset sky.

Subtle animation:

Moving ocean waves.
Palm leaves moving in the wind.

Unlock:

Win six matches.

ARENA 4: UNDERGROUND

Appearance:

Dark industrial warehouse.
Concrete walls.
Metal structures.
Underground fighting atmosphere.

Subtle animation:

Flickering lights.
Steam or environmental effects.

Unlock:

Win ten matches.

ARENA 5: SKY HIGH

Appearance:

City rooftop.
Large city skyline.
Buildings in the distance.
Nighttime atmosphere.

Subtle animation:

Moving clouds.
Distant city lights.

Unlock:

Win fifteen matches.

ARENA 6: FORGOTTEN TEMPLE

Appearance:

Ancient temple.
Mountain scenery.
Stone architecture.
Traditional decorations.

Subtle animation:

Moving leaves.
Gentle environmental effects.

Unlock:

Complete championship mode.

ARENA 7: THE COLOSSEUM

Appearance:

Ancient Roman gladiator arena.
Massive stone structures.
Spectator stands.
Roman banners.
Large cheering crowd.
Warm sunset lighting.

Subtle animation:

Cheering spectators.
Moving banners.
Environmental lighting effects.

Unlock:

Defeat the final championship boss.

ARENA REQUIREMENTS:

Every arena must have:

A distinct visual identity.
A separate background.
Proper fighting floor positioning.
Correct character scaling.
Unobstructed combat space.
Appropriate background music or ambient audio where practical.

Players must be able to revisit previously unlocked arenas.

================================================== SECTION 8: CHAMPIONSHIP MODE

Create a single-player championship mode.

The player selects one fighter and enters a fighting tournament.

The tournament must feature increasingly difficult opponents.

Include:

Tournament introduction.
Opponent presentation.
Individual fights.
Progression between matches.
Championship final.
Final victory screen.

The final boss should have stronger AI and a more challenging fighting style.

The Colosseum becomes available after the final boss is defeated.

The player must be able to replay championship mode.

Save championship completion and progression.

================================================== SECTION 9: COIN AND REWARD SYSTEM

Create a permanent in-game currency called LEGEND COINS.

Players earn coins by playing matches.

REWARDS:

Normal victory: 250 coins.

Victory without losing a round: 400 coins.

Perfect victory without taking damage: 600 coins.

Championship completion: 2,000 bonus coins.

Final boss defeat: 1,000 bonus coins.

Reward conditions must be checked correctly.

Do not award duplicate rewards from repeatedly opening a results screen.

The player's coin balance must be saved permanently.

The player must not lose coins when losing a match.

================================================== SECTION 10: IN-GAME SHOP

Create a shop called LEGENDS MARKET.

The shop must be fully functional.

The shop should have three main categories.

CATEGORY A: FIGHTER OUTFITS

Examples:

Alternate fighter costumes.
Different clothing colors.
Special outfits.
Rare outfits.
Exclusive championship costumes.

Suggested prices:

Standard alternate outfit: 1,000 coins.
Rare outfit: 2,500 coins.
Exclusive costume: 7,500 coins.

CATEGORY B: ACCESSORIES

Examples:

Gloves.
Boots.
Headbands.
Masks.
Hairstyles.

Suggested prices:

Gloves: 500 coins.
Boots: 750 coins.
Hairstyle: 800 coins.

CATEGORY C: FINISHING MOVES

Create unique finishing animations for fighters.

Examples:

Special knockout animations.
Unique final punches.
Unique final kicks.
Character-specific victory sequences.

Suggested price:

Special finishing move: 5,000 coins.

SHOP FUNCTIONALITY:

The player must be able to:

Browse categories.
View items.
Preview cosmetics.
See item prices.
Check their coin balance.
Purchase items.
Receive a purchase confirmation.
Equip unlocked items.
Unequip items.
Revisit purchased items.

PURCHASE RULES:

All items must be purchased using earned Legend Coins.
No additional real-money purchases.
No paid loot boxes.
No advertisements.
No subscriptions.
No randomized paid rewards.
No duplicate purchases for already owned items.

Purchased items must remain permanently unlocked.

The shop must never subtract coins without completing a successful purchase.

================================================== SECTION 11: MAIN MENU AND GAME INTERFACE

Create an attractive retro arcade main menu.

MAIN MENU OPTIONS:

PLAY
CHAMPIONSHIP
FIGHTERS
LEGENDS MARKET
ARENA SELECT
SETTINGS

The main menu should display:

Street Legends logo.
Animated fighter artwork.
Player coin balance.
Clear navigation buttons.

CHARACTER SELECTION:

Display all available fighters.

Show:

Fighter portrait.
Fighter name.
Fighting style.
Statistics.
Special move.
Locked or unlocked status.

Allow the player to preview a character before choosing.

ARENA SELECTION:

Display the seven arenas.

Show:

Arena preview.
Arena name.
Unlock requirement.
Locked or unlocked status.

RESULTS SCREEN:

After every match, display:

Winner.
Loser.
Rounds won.
Match performance.
Coins earned.
Updated coin balance.

Include buttons for:

Rematch.
Return to main menu.
Continue championship, when applicable.
================================================== SECTION 12: SOUND AND MUSIC

Include:

Main menu music.
Fighting music.
Different music or ambient sound for arenas where possible.
Punch sound effects.
Kick sound effects.
Blocking sound effects.
Jump sound effects.
Knockout sound effects.
Victory music.
Defeat music.
Menu navigation sounds.
Shop purchase confirmation sounds.

Audio must be compressed and optimized.

Include separate volume controls for:

Music.
Sound effects.

Allow players to mute audio.

Use original or properly licensed audio assets.

================================================== SECTION 13: SAVE SYSTEM

Create a reliable local save system.

Save:

Player coin balance.
Unlocked characters.
Purchased outfits.
Purchased accessories.
Purchased finishing moves.
Equipped cosmetics.
Unlocked arenas.
Championship completion.
Match progression.
Settings.
Sound preferences.

Progress must remain saved after:

Closing the game.
Restarting the application.
Losing a match.
Returning to the main menu.

Use appropriate local storage for the development platform.

Avoid resetting player progress when entering a new match.

Handle interrupted purchases and interrupted matches safely.

================================================== SECTION 14: MONETIZATION AND APP STORE MODEL

BUSINESS MODEL:

The game must be sold for a one-time purchase price of $0.99.

This price is intended for the initial App Store release and must be configured through the appropriate store listing and pricing system.

The game must be a complete premium product.

STRICT MONETIZATION RULES:

No advertisements.
No rewarded advertisements.
No banner advertisements.
No forced video advertisements.
No additional paid characters.
No additional paid outfits.
No paid finishing moves.
No subscriptions.
No additional in-game real-money purchases.

All cosmetic items must be obtainable through gameplay and Legend Coins.

The game should be playable offline after installation wherever the platform permits.

Do not introduce advertising SDKs or unnecessary third-party services.

================================================== SECTION 15: DOWNLOAD SIZE AND PERFORMANCE

The game must be lightweight.

TARGET DOWNLOAD SIZE: 50–80 MB.

MAXIMUM TARGET: Under 100 MB.

This is a target that must be verified after export, not an assumed result.

OPTIMIZATION:

Compress image assets.
Use optimized pixel-art spritesheets.
Reuse suitable visual assets.
Compress music and sound effects.
Avoid unnecessary video files.
Avoid unnecessary high-resolution textures.
Remove unused assets.
Avoid unnecessarily large libraries.
Optimize animations and backgrounds.

Do not sacrifice fighter detail to reduce file size.

PERFORMANCE:

Target 60 FPS on supported devices.
Maintain responsive touchscreen controls.
Avoid excessive memory usage.
Prevent unnecessary loading screens.
Keep gameplay smooth.
Avoid crashes during matches or shop interactions.
================================================== SECTION 16: MOBILE USER EXPERIENCE

Design the entire interface for mobile devices.

Requirements:

Landscape orientation.
Readable text.
Large touchscreen buttons.
Appropriate spacing.
Clear health bars.
Visible countdown timer.
Easy-to-use menus.
Responsive layout.
Proper screen scaling.

Do not place important buttons too close to screen edges.

Ensure the controls do not cover the fighters.

================================================== SECTION 17: QUALITY ASSURANCE AND TESTING

Before considering the game complete, test every major feature.

COMBAT TESTS:

Movement works in both directions.
Jumping works.
Crouching works.
Punches connect correctly.
Kicks connect correctly.
Blocking works.
Special moves activate correctly.
Health decreases correctly.
Knockouts work.
Match winners are determined correctly.
Round progression works.

AI TESTS:

Opponents move.
Opponents attack.
Opponents defend.
Opponents use special moves.
Difficulty levels behave differently.

SHOP TESTS:

Coins are awarded correctly.
Coins are saved.
Purchases work.
Insufficient funds prevent purchases.
Owned items cannot be purchased twice.
Cosmetics can be equipped.
Cosmetics remain unlocked after restarting.

ARENA TESTS:

All seven backgrounds load correctly.
Unlock requirements work.
Locked arenas cannot be entered.
Unlocked arenas can be replayed.

SAVE TESTS:

Close and reopen the game.
Confirm coin balance remains correct.
Confirm purchases remain unlocked.
Confirm arena progression remains saved.
Confirm championship completion remains saved.

PERFORMANCE TESTS:

Check for crashes.
Check for missing assets.
Check for distorted sprites.
Check for broken animations.
Check mobile controls.
Measure the exported installation size.
================================================== SECTION 18: DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES

Build the game in the following order.

PHASE 1: Create the core fighting engine, player movement, attacks, hit detection, health bars, timer, and AI opponent.

PHASE 2: Create the four initial fighters with their unique appearances, animations, statistics, and special moves.

PHASE 3: Create all seven arenas and the arena selection system.

PHASE 4: Create the championship tournament and final boss.

PHASE 5: Create Legend Coins, match rewards, and the complete Legends Market.

PHASE 6: Implement outfit customization, accessories, and finishing moves.

PHASE 7: Create the main menu, character selection, results screens, audio, and settings.

PHASE 8: Implement permanent saving and loading.

PHASE 9: Optimize assets, test gameplay, fix bugs, and export the final mobile build.

IMPORTANT DEVELOPMENT INSTRUCTIONS:

Do not skip requested features.
Do not replace functional mechanics with decorative buttons.
Do not create fake shop purchases.
Do not make every fighter look identical.
Do not use tiny character sprites.
Do not remove any of the seven arenas.
Do not add advertisements.
Do not add additional real-money purchases.
Do not sacrifice gameplay quality for unnecessary visual effects.

If a requested feature cannot be implemented by the available development tools, clearly identify the limitation rather than pretending the feature works.

Prioritize a stable, complete, playable game over unnecessary complexity.

FINAL GOAL:

Deliver STREET LEGENDS as a polished, lightweight, premium 2D arcade fighting game with large detailed pixel-art fighters, responsive combat, seven unique arenas, a championship mode, an earnable coin economy, and a fully functional cosmetic shop.

The game should feel like a complete classic arcade fighting experience redesigned for modern mobile devices.Character size: The fighters must actually look large on the screen. Don't let the AI interpret pixel art as tiny 32 × 32 characters.
The shop: Make sure purchases, coin deductions, and saved outfits work. A shop that only looks attractive isn't enough.
Seven arenas: Check that all seven are separate selectable stages, not seven names attached to the same background.
File size: Check the exported build, not just the project size displayed inside the editor.
4. A realistic development expectation


If it struggles, prioritize these features in order:

Working one-versus-one combat.
Four functional fighters.
Seven backgrounds.
Championship progression.
Working coin system.
Working shop.
Cosmetics and finishing moves.Category	Number
Male fighters	10

Total playable fighters	20
Initially available	4
Unlockable	16MAJOR ROSTER EXPANSION: 20 PLAYABLE FIGHTERS

Expand STREET LEGENDS to feature a complete roster of 20 original playable fighters.

ROSTER COMPOSITION:

10 male fighters.
10 female fighters.
All characters must be adults.
All characters must have unique appearances.
All characters must have individual fighting styles.
All characters must have their own special moves.
All characters must be selectable and playable.

MALE FIGHTERS:

Kenji — Karate — Dragon Strike.
Bruno — Boxing — Heavy Impact.
Jae — Taekwondo — Lightning Kick.
Marcus — Street Fighting — Ground Breaker.
Ryuji — Kenjutsu — Blade Dance.

FEMALE FIGHTERS:

Maya — Kickboxing — Cyclone Kick.
Akari — Ninjutsu — Shadow Rush.
Scarlett — Boxing — Crimson Knockout.
Nia — Taekwondo — Skybreaker.
Mei — Kung Fu — Golden Dragon.

Raven — Wrestling — Raven's Wrath.
Yuna — Kenjutsu — Moonlight Strike.
Vanessa — Street Fighting — Street Fury.
Seraphina — Mystic Martial Arts — Celestial Burst.

CHARACTER APPEARANCE:

Create visually attractive, detailed and recognizable adult characters.

Female character design:

Attractive facial features.
Distinctive hairstyles.
Athletic physiques.
Stylish fighting outfits.
Individual color palettes.
Detailed clothing and accessories.
Confident and memorable personalities.

Male character design:

Distinctive facial features.
Different hairstyles.
Varied body types.
Detailed fighting uniforms and streetwear.
Unique fighting stances.
Individual color palettes.

Do not make characters look identical.

Do not simply recolor one character sprite to create another fighter.

CHARACTER ANIMATIONS:

Every fighter must have:

Idle animation.
Walking animation.
Jumping animation.
Crouching animation.
Punch animation.
Kick animation.
Blocking animation.
Hit reaction.
Knockdown animation.
Getting-up animation.
Special attack animation.
Finishing move animation.
Victory animation.
Defeat animation.

Every fighter must have unique special attacks and recognizable finishing moves.

CHARACTER STATISTICS:

Each character must have individual:

Health.
Attack strength.
Defense.
Movement speed.
Jump height.
Special attack power.

Ensure balanced competitive gameplay.

UNLOCK SYSTEM:

Four fighters are available initially: Kenji, Bruno, Maya and Akari.

The remaining 16 fighters must be unlockable through gameplay.

Use championship progression and Legend Coins to unlock fighters.

Display locked characters in the character selection menu.

Show each locked fighter's name, portrait, fighting style and unlock requirement.

Do not charge real money for fighters.

CUSTOMIZATION:

Every fighter should support at least two additional unlockable outfits.

Allow players to equip outfits and accessories from Legends Market.

Outfits must not change character hitboxes, damage values or competitive balance.

IMPORTANT TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS:

Create individual character assets.
Use optimized spritesheets.
Reuse suitable animation infrastructure without making characters visually identical.
Maintain consistent sprite scale.
Preserve large, detailed character appearances.
Optimize character assets to help keep the total game installation below 100 MB.

All 20 fighters must be included in the final playable roster.

Do not silently reduce the roster to four or eight characters.

If the development environment cannot generate all 20 at once, build them in organized batches while preserving the complete 20-character roster design and character selection system.Touchscreen Controls – Essential Requirement

Create a fully functional, responsive touchscreen control layout for mobile devices in landscape orientation.

Left side – Movement controls
Add a large virtual directional joystick on the bottom-left of the screen.
The joystick must support moving left, right, jumping (up), and crouching (down).
Alternatively, provide four separate directional arrow buttons if a virtual joystick is not supported.
The joystick must respond smoothly and immediately to finger movement.
Keep it fixed in position so players can easily reach it with their left thumb.
Right side – Action buttons

Add four large, clearly labeled arcade-style buttons:

X – Punch: Fast standard punch attack.
A – Kick: Standard kick attack.
B – Block: Hold to defend against incoming attacks.
Y – Special: Perform the character's unique special move when enough special meter is available.

Buttons must respond to touch and support holding where appropriate. Each button must trigger its assigned fighting action reliably.

Additional requirements
Display all controls directly over the gameplay screen.
Use large, clearly visible buttons with distinct colors and recognizable labels.
Make buttons comfortable to press without accidentally touching neighboring buttons.
Allow simultaneous inputs where appropriate, such as moving while attacking or jumping while kicking.
Prevent controls from covering the fighters, health bars, timer, or important gameplay information.
Make the control layout scale correctly across different phone and tablet screen sizes.
Provide an option in Settings to adjust control size and transparency.
Ensure controls work through actual touchscreen input, not just keyboard simulation.
Do not require a physical controller or keyboard to play.
Test every control on a real touchscreen device before release.Fighter Collision, Solid Movement and Living Environments
1. Solid Fighter Collision – Essential

Characters must behave like solid physical objects during combat.

Fighters must never walk through, overlap, or pass through each other.
Implement proper collision detection and collision boundaries between both fighters.
When fighters approach each other, they must stop at a realistic fighting distance.
If one fighter pushes toward the other, prevent them from moving through their opponent.
Characters must maintain consistent ground positioning and must not slide, teleport, or randomly drift.
Jumping, crouching, blocking, attacking, knockbacks, and special moves must respect collision rules.
Knockback animations must not cause fighters to pass through one another.
Prevent fighters from leaving the playable arena boundaries.
Ensure collision detection works consistently at different frame rates.
Use separate attack hitboxes and character collision boxes so attacks can connect without sprites physically passing through each other.
Both fighters must remain properly grounded unless jumping or being knocked into the air.
2. Living Backgrounds and Environmental Animations

Make every arena feel alive instead of using completely static backgrounds.

Add subtle environmental animations that do not interfere with fighting or reduce performance.

Examples:

Birds flying across the sky and occasionally landing on rooftops.
Birds taking off from buildings and flying away.
Clouds slowly moving across the sky.
Trees, palm leaves, and plants gently moving in the wind.
Streetlights flickering and neon signs glowing.
Windows and buildings displaying changing lights.
Ocean waves moving and crashing on the beach.
Flags and banners gently waving.
Dust, steam, and leaves moving through appropriate environments.
Background spectators occasionally cheering, clapping, and moving.

Each arena should have environmental animations appropriate to its setting. Do not simply reuse the same background effects everywhere.

3. Dynamic Day and Night Cycle

Implement a visual day-and-night cycle for arenas.

Gradually transition between morning, daytime, evening, sunset, and nighttime.
Change the sky color, lighting, shadows, and environmental atmosphere.
The sun should move across the sky during daytime.
The sun should set and the moon should appear at night.
Stars should become visible in suitable nighttime environments.
Clouds should continue moving during the cycle.
City lights and streetlights should turn on as darkness approaches and turn off during daylight.
Beach sunsets should have changing sky colors and lighting.
Background environments should visually respond to the time of day.
4. Cycle Settings and Performance
Allow players to select a fixed time of day or enable automatic day/night cycling.
Make transitions gradual and smooth, not sudden.
Keep the fighting area bright enough to see characters and attacks clearly.
Environmental animations must never interfere with combat hitboxes or controls.
Optimize background animations to maintain the target 60 FPS.
Do not sacrifice fighter sprite quality or animation detail for background effects.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.

## Objective
- Build a complete, polished, lightweight mobile 2D pixel-art fighting game, **STREET LEGENDS**, in the existing project; do not deliver only a visual demo or disconnected menus.

## Requirements
- Landscape, side-view, single-player arcade fighting; target 60 FPS and under 100 MB exported size, ideally 50–80 MB; one-time $0.99 premium release with no ads or additional real-money purchases.
- Twenty playable adult fighters (10 male, 10 female): Kenji, Bruno, Jae, Marcus, Ryuji, Axel, Titan, Liang, Dante, Vex; Maya, Akari, Scarlett, Nia, Mei, Isabella, Raven, Yuna, Vanessa, Seraphina. Kenji, Bruno, Maya, and Akari start unlocked; unlock the other 16 through gameplay and/or Legend Coins. Each needs distinct appearance, style, special move, stats, animations, and at least two unlockable outfits.
- Functional combat: real hitboxes, solid fighter collision, movement boundaries, attacks, blocks, specials, combos, health, knockback, stun, jumping/crouching, rounds, 60-second timer, first-to-two matches, and AI with Easy/Normal/Hard difficulty.
- Functional touchscreen controls: bottom-left joystick or directional buttons; right-side X punch, A kick, B hold-to-block, Y special; simultaneous inputs, responsive touch, scalable layout, adjustable size/transparency in Settings, and real-device testing before release.
- Seven genuinely distinct selectable arenas with gameplay-safe floor/camera composition, appropriate environmental animation, unlock requirements, and fixed or automatic gradual day/night cycle. Maintain visibility and performance.
- Championship progression with increasingly difficult opponents and a final boss; persistent completion and arena unlocks.
- Earnable Legend Coins, correctly checked match/championship rewards, permanent local save, and a working Legends Market for outfits, accessories, and finishing moves. Prevent duplicate purchases and incorrect deductions; purchases/equipped items persist.
- Main menu, character and arena selection, results, settings/audio controls, compressed original or licensed audio, and robust local saves.
- Test core combat, AI, controls, all arenas, shop, progression, saves, and exported installation size; clearly disclose any platform/tool limitations.

## Decisions
- Prioritize a stable playable game, in order: combat, four functional fighters, seven distinct backgrounds, championship progression, coin system, working shop, then cosmetics and finishing moves.
- Use reasonable assumptions without asking follow-up questions; briefly note assumptions at completion.

1. Inspect the existing project and identify its engine, current implementation, and test/build workflow.

3. Run available tests and builds; verify touchscreen support, saved shop transactions, and exported size where feasible, and report unverified real-device testing clearly.

- User explicitly emphasizes large, detailed fighters (not tiny 32×32 sprites), real functional shop purchases and persistence, seven separate arena backgrounds, and measuring exported build size rather than relying on editor estimates.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete STREET LEGENDS as a playable, mobile-first 2D arcade fighting game within the existing project, preserving its 20-fighter roster, seven arenas, championship progression, touchscreen combat, and coin shop.

## Requirements
- Landscape, side-view single-player combat with detailed pixel-art fighters; target 60 FPS and exported size under 100 MB.
- Include 20 adult fighters (10 male, 10 female) with distinct style, special, stats, and appearance; Kenji, Bruno, Maya, and Akari start unlocked.
- Implement combat, collision, AI difficulty, rounds/timer, combos, blocking, specials, responsive touch controls with adjustable size/transparency, and keyboard input.
- Include seven selectable animated arenas with day/night lighting and unlock progression.
- Implement championship mode, persistent coins/progression, working local-save shop with purchases/equipping, menus, and audio/settings controls.
- No ads or additional real-money purchases; one-time $0.99 premium release model.
- Test where feasible and disclose unverified real-device and build limitations; make reasonable assumptions without follow-up.

## Decisions
- Prioritize stable combat, fighters, arenas, championship, economy, and shop before cosmetics and finishers.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` includes the 20-fighter roster, seven arena renderers, menu/panel markup and rendering, and initial local-save state structure.
- Added screen functions for roster, arena, shop, and settings panels; match setup, HUD updates, and tournament opponent/progression scaffolding.

### Active
- Finish and wire gameplay systems in `index.html`: combat/input loop, match and round resolution, rewards, tournament progression, shop transactions, settings, and event handlers.
- Verify functionality, responsive play, saves, arenas, and exported size where feasible.

### Blocked
- `index.html` currently ends after `toast(text)` without closing the script/document; numerous referenced functions/IDs and required event wiring are still missing.

## Next Move
1. Continue `index.html` after `toast(text)` with combat simulation, input handlers, AI, rounds, match outcomes/rewards, tournament flow, shop logic, and settings persistence.
2. Check missing HTML/script structure and referenced DOM elements; run the app and resolve JavaScript/runtime errors.
3. Test core gameplay, saves/purchases, arena selections, and responsive controls; inspect a screenshot and measure export size if available.
4. Report assumptions and any unverified device/build limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Single-file game implementation; current work and incomplete script tail.

## Important Context
- Latest code ends at `function toast(text){...}` on line 125; closing `</script>` and `</body></html>` are absent.
- Existing code calls undefined functions including `applyControlSettings()`; match and UI event handlers are not yet wired.
- `showHome()` references `matchresult`, and `startMatch()` references `hud`, controls, and `message`; these elements exist in the current HTML.
- Changes are uncommitted.

- Complete STREET LEGENDS as a playable, mobile-first 2D arcade fighting game within the existing project, preserving its roster, arenas, championship progression, touchscreen combat, and coin shop.

## Requirements
- Landscape, side-view single-player combat; detailed pixel-art fighters; target 60 FPS and exported size under 100 MB.
- Include 20 adult fighters (10 male, 10 female) with distinct styles, specials, stats, and appearances; Kenji, Bruno, Maya, and Akari start unlocked.
- Implement combat, collision, AI difficulty, rounds/timer, combos, blocking, specials, responsive adjustable touch controls, and keyboard input.
- Include seven selectable animated arenas with day/night lighting and unlock progression.
- Implement championship mode, persistent coins/progression, working local-save shop with purchases/equipping, menus, and audio/settings controls.
- No ads or additional real-money purchases; one-time $0.99 premium release model.
- Test where feasible and disclose unverified real-device and build limitations; make reasonable assumptions without follow-up.

## Decisions
- Prioritize stable combat, fighters, arenas, championship, economy, and shop before cosmetics and finishers.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` now contains the complete single-file game UI, 20-fighter roster, seven animated arenas, and pixel-art fighter rendering.
- Added local persistence, fighter unlocks, arena progression, quick fights, championship scaffolding, rounds, timer, combat/AI, rewards, coin shop, settings, touch and keyboard controls, and synthesized sound effects.
- Restored script/document closure and verified JavaScript syntax with `node --check /tmp/game.js`.
- Chromium headless opened the file and produced `/tmp/street-home.png`; file size is 49,958 bytes.

### Active
- Validate gameplay, combat edge cases, persistence, shop operations, menu navigation, responsiveness, and runtime errors in-browser.
- Review collision/round handling and championship progression for correctness; determine whether any fixes are needed.

### Blocked
- Real-device testing and packaged/export build verification have not been performed.

## Next Move
1. Run browser-driven interaction tests for starting fights, controls, round/match completion, rewards, unlocks, shop purchases/equipping, and save reload.
2. Inspect the screenshot and test at mobile landscape and desktop viewports; fix any issues found.
3. Confirm export size/build constraints where feasible, then report test coverage and unverified real-device/build limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh` as untracked.
- `applyControlSettings()` is declared twice in the script; both versions currently set touch-control opacity and scale.
- Chromium headless generated a screenshot; its stderr included system DBus/UPower errors, not an observed game error.

## Objective
- Complete STREET LEGENDS as a playable, mobile-first 2D arcade fighting game within the existing project, preserving its roster, arenas, championship progression, touchscreen combat, and coin shop.

## Requirements
- Landscape, side-view single-player combat; detailed pixel-art fighters; target 60 FPS and exported size under 100 MB.
- Include 20 adult fighters (10 male, 10 female) with distinct styles, specials, stats, and appearances; Kenji, Bruno, Maya, and Akari start unlocked.
- Implement combat, collision, AI difficulty, rounds/timer, combos, blocking, specials, responsive adjustable touch controls, and keyboard input.
- Include seven selectable animated arenas with day/night lighting and unlock progression.
- Implement championship mode, persistent coins/progression, working local-save shop with purchases/equipping, menus, and audio/settings controls.
- No ads or additional real-money purchases; one-time $0.99 premium release model.
- Test where feasible and disclose unverified real-device and build limitations; make reasonable assumptions without follow-up.

## Decisions
- Prioritize stable combat, fighters, arenas, championship, economy, and shop before cosmetics and finishers.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` contains the single-file game UI, 20-fighter roster, seven animated arenas, persistence, progression, quick fights, championship scaffolding, combat/AI, shop, settings, touch/keyboard controls, and synthesized sound effects.
- JavaScript syntax checked successfully with `node --check /tmp/game.js`; game loaded in Chromium via local HTTP server.
- Browser smoke test confirmed the home screen and Quick Fight launch, HUD, fighter names, and eight touch controls.

### Active
- Validate gameplay, combat edge cases, persistence, shop operations, menu navigation, responsiveness, and runtime errors in-browser.
- Review collision/round handling and championship progression; fix issues found.
- Check export-size/build constraints where feasible.

### Blocked
- Real-device testing and packaged/export build verification have not been performed.

## Next Move
1. Continue browser-driven tests for combat, match completion/rewards, progression, shop purchases/equipping, and save reload.
2. Check desktop and mobile-landscape layouts and runtime errors; address gameplay or UI issues found.
3. Check export-size/build constraints if feasible, then report coverage and remaining limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete game implementation.
- `README.md`: Project overview and build-run links.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh` as untracked.
- `applyControlSettings()` is defined twice in `index.html`.
- Browser’s only console error observed was a missing `/favicon.ico` (404), not a game runtime error.
- Browser interaction was launched at `http://127.0.0.1:8765/index.html`; viewport was resized to 844×390 but no further mobile checks completed.

## Objective
- Complete STREET LEGENDS as a playable, mobile-first 2D arcade fighting game within the existing project, preserving its roster, arenas, championship progression, touchscreen combat, and coin shop.

## Requirements
- Landscape, side-view single-player combat; detailed pixel-art fighters; target 60 FPS and exported size under 100 MB.
- Include 20 adult fighters (10 male, 10 female) with distinct styles, specials, stats, and appearances; Kenji, Bruno, Maya, and Akari start unlocked.
- Implement combat, collision, AI difficulty, rounds/timer, combos, blocking, specials, responsive adjustable touch controls, and keyboard input.
- Include seven selectable animated arenas with day/night lighting and unlock progression.
- Implement championship mode, persistent coins/progression, working local-save shop with purchases/equipping, menus, and audio/settings controls.
- No ads or additional real-money purchases; one-time $0.99 premium release model.
- Test where feasible and disclose unverified real-device and build limitations; make reasonable assumptions without follow-up.

## Decisions
- Prioritize stable combat, fighters, arenas, championship, economy, and shop before cosmetics and finishers.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` contains the game UI, 20-fighter roster, seven arenas, persistence/progression, quick fights, championship, combat/AI, shop, settings, touch/keyboard controls, and synthesized sound effects.

- Real-device testing and packaged/export build verification have not been performed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete STREET LEGENDS as a playable, mobile-first 2D arcade fighting game within the existing project.
- Preserve its roster, arenas, championship progression, touchscreen combat, and coin shop.

## Requirements
- Landscape, side-view single-player combat; detailed pixel-art fighters; target 60 FPS and exported size under 100 MB.
- Include 20 adult fighters (10 male, 10 female) with distinct styles, specials, stats, and appearances; Kenji, Bruno, Maya, and Akari start unlocked.
- Implement combat, collision, AI difficulty, rounds/timer, combos, blocking, specials, adjustable touch controls, and keyboard input.
- Include seven selectable animated arenas with day/night lighting and unlock progression.
- Implement championship mode, persistent coins/progression, working local-save shop with purchases/equipping, menus, and audio/settings controls.
- No ads or additional real-money purchases; one-time $0.99 premium release model.
- Test where feasible and disclose unverified real-device and build limitations; make reasonable assumptions without follow-up.

## Decisions
- Prioritize stable combat, fighters, arenas, championship, economy, and shop before cosmetics and finishers.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` implements the game UI, 20-fighter roster, seven arenas, persistence/progression, quick fights, championship, combat/AI, shop, settings, touch/keyboard controls, and synthesized sound effects.
- Browser checks confirmed home/match UI, touch controls in bounds at 844×390 at default scale, punches damage, blocking mitigates damage, attacks build meter, and match victory rewards persist.
- Fixed shop accessory purchases/equipping and added visual accessory rendering; outfit palettes and accessories persist across reloads.
- Fixed touch controls being hidden after a match when starting a new fight; removed a duplicate `applyControlSettings()` definition.
- Tested six championship wins: champion/boss flags and final two arenas unlock, and no next-bout button appears after completion.
- Tested shop purchases/equipping, save persistence, and touch controls after returning to a new fight.
- Fixed keyboard block state to clear correctly on keyup and added an empty data favicon to avoid the prior `/favicon.ico` 404.
- Tested a round transition and match victory flow in-browser; JavaScript syntax check passed; `index.html` is approximately 50 KB, below the 100 MB target.
- Latest browser console check reported no errors after favicon fix.

### Active
- Fix max-size touch-control scaling: at 844×390, setting `save.settings.control` to `1.3` clips left/up/down controls off the left edge and the special button off the right edge.
- Finish testing arena/fighter selection, settings persistence, collision behavior, and mobile/desktop layouts.
- Verify export/build expectations where the project supports them.

### Blocked
- Real-device testing and packaged/export build verification have not been performed.

## Next Move
1. Adjust `applyControlSettings()` or control layout so all touch controls remain in bounds at the maximum setting and on narrow screens; retest at 844×390 and other viewport sizes.
2. Complete remaining navigation, settings persistence, and gameplay checks; investigate/fix defects found.
3. Check build/export support and report verification limits; note finishers remain collectibles without combat effects.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game implementation and recent fixes.
- `README.md`: Project overview and run/build links.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` lists `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh` as untracked.
- Accessories can be equipped and displayed; finishers remain collectibles without combat effects.
- Browser test URL: `http://127.0.0.1:8765/index.html`; a local Python HTTP server was running during testing.

STREET LEGENDS – COMPLETE CHARACTER REDESIGN AND GAMEPLAY REVISION

IMPORTANT: This is a revision of the existing Street Legends project. Preserve the existing game, menus, progression, touchscreen controls, arenas, currency, and save system. Do not restart or remove existing features.

The current game has several problems that must be corrected.

Characters look like Minecraft characters.
Characters have insufficient fighting animations.
Enemy AI does not fight back.
The day/night cycle progresses too quickly.

The priority is to make Street Legends look and play like a genuine 1990s arcade fighting game.

1. COMPLETE REDESIGN OF ALL 20 CHARACTERS

Redesign the entire roster from scratch visually.

Do not simply change colors or clothing on the existing blocky characters.

Required visual art style

Use detailed 16-bit pixel-art fighting-game sprites inspired by classic 1990s arcade fighters.

Characters must have:

Realistic human-shaped anatomy in a stylized arcade art style.
Properly proportioned heads, torsos, arms, hands, legs, and feet.
Attractive, recognizable faces with detailed eyes, noses, and mouths.
Detailed hairstyles with individual pixel clusters.
Athletic and naturally proportioned physiques.
Detailed clothing with folds, shading, highlights, and texture.
Smooth silhouettes and carefully outlined body shapes.
Detailed hands and feet instead of square blocks.
Unique fighting stances and recognizable personalities.

STRICTLY PROHIBITED:

Minecraft-style characters.
Voxel characters.
Cube-shaped heads or limbs.
Blocky rectangular bodies.
Stick figures.
Generic low-detail characters.
Static character images pretending to be animations.
